analysis.title: GS Joseph - GS Macro Reads 25 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS FX (Trivedi) sees dollar performance mixed and contained in a challenging week for markets. Terms of trade drive returns under the surface: AUD, CAD and NOK led on higher energy prices, and KRW benefited from AI demand.

GS frames the market as debating two tail scenarios. Scenario one: US tech headlines signal slower, smaller capex with tighter corporate credit conditions, negative for the broad Dollar and positive for the Yen. Scenario two: a short-lived recalibration with sovereign credit concerns re-emerging in Europe, negative for EUR and positive for USD and KRW. GS thinks the latter is more likely and says FX can hedge both.

GS baseline: inflation pressures moderate, growth cools somewhat, G10 policy stays synchronized. This argues for low FX vol and a slightly weaker Dollar, particularly against high-carry EM currencies or firmly managed ones such as CNY.

GS (Cahill) argues the Yen is a more attractive hedge for procyclical portfolios than in recent years. Domestic policy is turning more constructive and intervention risk limits depreciation, which adds downside asymmetry to USD/JPY. The Yen benefits most when equities and yields fall together.

GS tactically favors EUR funding across currencies including JPY (short EUR/JPY). The BoJ meeting on October 30 faces a high bar to surprise hawkishly versus market pricing. Longer term, short USD/JPY is the most effective hedge against growth wobbles or an AI shock.

GS (Suwanapruti) sees CNY appreciating steadily, approaching the 3m USD/CNY target of 6.70, with offshore spot already stronger than that. China's September trade surplus was US$133.5bn (NSA), the largest monthly surplus on record. GS targets USD/CNY at 6.40 in 12m and says consensus and forwards underestimate the move.

GS is bullish TWD for the medium term after recent underperformance. Net foreign equity outflows from Taiwan were USD 26bn in October, and TSMC's October dividend is USD 5.7bn, about USD 4bn of it to overseas investors. GS expects a record current account surplus of 24% of GDP in 2026 and forecasts USD/TWD at 32.0 (3M), 31.50 (6M) and 31.0 (12M).

GS rates (Marshall) says the risk-off tone has turned the tide for global duration ahead of late October and early November central bank decisions. GS anchors a long bias in the belly of the curve and prefers flatteners such as 2s5s in core Euro area rates.

GS expects the UK Autumn Budget to focus on maturity mix more than issuance size, which favors swap spread longs. In JGBs, GS expects bearish pressure from the 5y sector with multiple routes to flattening.

GS economists expect the BoC, RBA and RBNZ each to hike at upcoming meetings. GS sees cumulative hike pricing as excessive in Canada and New Zealand given slack, and sees clearer value in front-end flatteners in Australia.

GS Prime: US equities were net sold for a third straight week (4 of the last 5), with single stocks seeing the largest de-grossing since late July. Staples and Real Estate were the most net bought sectors, pointing to a defensive posture.
GS floor flow: about $20bn of net TMT selling across all client types over two weeks, approaching the -$23bn seen over two weeks in the July AI selling episode.
Managed Money added $2.3bn of new gross longs in Brent from October 6-13, 32% of it calls. Dealers and market makers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Thursday saw capitulation and de-grossing on AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record to its lowest since April of last year. The NDX vs SPX implied vol spread is near 5-year highs (98th percentile).

GS baskets view: the market is in a hedge fund deleveraging episode where short-term stops matter more than medium-term value. GS says to buy the dip and selectively reposition into AI starting with Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage on a beta-adjusted basis is down 21 pts from the June highs and near 3-year lows (5th percentile).

GS (Hatzius): S&P Global US services PMI edged down in October and manufacturing PMI was roughly unchanged. Activity is healthy but not surging, and manufacturing input and output prices rose sharply.

GS now expects Taiwan's central bank to begin a hike cycle in December 2026, raising policy rate forecasts to 2.125% for end-2026 and 2.375% for end-2027 (from 2.0%). Corporate loan growth reached 12.4% in mid-2026, the fastest since 1998.
GS raised its Taiwan Q3 real GDP forecast to 0.8% qoq sa (from 0.5%) for the Oct 30 release, and expects Korea Q3 real GDP of +0.5% qoq sa on Oct 27.
